en: The Brief Method for the Recitation of the *Yogācārabhūmi* by Maitreya Bodhisattva, Volume One.
From the *All-Sūtras of the Shōrin-in at Seiryū-ji Temple*.
Chapter One: The Five Great Contemplation Gates for Entering the Dharma Realm; The Five Great Contemplation Gates for Entering the Dharma Realm by Maitreya Bodhisattva.
I prostrate to the Buddha Vairocana, the Maitreya who is in his final birth before Buddhahood,
the four wisdoms, the four pāramitās, the eight great beings (mahāsattvas),
and the male and female forms of the vidyās of the five families, representing the characteristics of samādhi and prajñā.
To the hosts of World-Protecting Heavenly Kings of the ten directions, I now prostrate with my head to all of them.
For the benefit of all, I cultivate the *yūgī*; may I swiftly accomplish the great *siddhi* of Maitreya.
To cultivate the unborn, I speak the *yūga*; desiring to seek that which has signs, I speak of signs as well.
Existence and non-existence are two aspects of a single essence;
The three—text, contemplation, and the wisdom of the true mark—destroy the signless through the six pāramitās. The actions of body, speech, and mind constitute the three secrets;
These three secrets immediately become the dharmas of response and transformation; The five wheels and five wisdoms are the five divisions.
The five parts completely encompass the wheel of the Dharma-realm; therefore, I now pay homage to Maitreya.
Maitreya is the Honored One of Loving-kindness (Maitreya); therefore, I now cultivate Maitreya so that I may swiftly realize the same single essence as Maitreya.
If one wishes not to relinquish the physical body in this present life, [one should practice thus].
Those who wish to swiftly realize the palace of Maitreya, to assemble there together to hear the Dharma,
and to attain great *siddhi*,
must certainly rely upon this *yogini* for their recitation.
One will certainly attain the unsurpassed great siddhi.
If one wishes to perform recitation according to this rite,
one should first contemplate the samaya of the pure dharmadhātu-mind.
At the crown of the head is the wheel of the fire of wisdom, resembling the sun just as it rises;
its color is brilliant and its shape is triangular.
The maṇḍala is shaped as shown on the left.
The mantra of the mind of the pure *dharmadhātu* is:
*Namaḥ samantabhadra*. (1) Recite this once; as at the crown of the head, visualize a triangular fire of wisdom that completely incinerates the entire body.
The five aggregates are all empty; there is only emptiness and stillness.
From within this, one contemplates the Vajrāsana;
from the waist downward, it is of purple-gold color.
The form of the vajra-wheel is as shown on the left.
The mantra of the vajra-wheel is called the Vajracakra-āsana.
From above the vajra-circle, one contemplates the water-circle.
Its color is white like śaṅkha;
its shape is like the full moon, and its form is circular to the left.
The mantra of the Water Wheel is:
Na-maḥ samanta-bha-dra-nā-ma-śrī. This is called the Water Wheel. Recite it once.
Furthermore, from the center of the water wheel, one should visualize the fire wheel of wisdom at the heart.
It is triangular, red in color, with its apex pointing upward,
and is called the "Mind of All-Knowledge."
Its form is as follows.
The mantra of the Fire Wheel is:
NA-MA-SA-MAN-TA-BHA-TA-NAM (1) RAṂ (2). Recite this once more. Furthermore, visualize above the eyebrows a crescent moon in the shape of an upward-facing wheel.
If black winds gather like overhanging clouds,
and their form is as follows on the left,
the mantra of the wind-wheel is:
Namaḥ samantabhadra-nātha (1). (2) Recite this once more. Furthermore, visualize the syllable *khaṃ* at the crown of the head as space.
Possessing all colors,
its form is as shown on the left.
The mantra of the Space Wheel (*ākāśacakra*) is as follows:
Namaḥ samantabhadra nātha. (1) [The second is] Vajra. (2) First, draw the five wheels as shown in the diagram to the left.
Visualize the five wheels and the Dharma-realm eye diagram as described above.
Adorn the body with the wheels of the five wisdoms.
Empower the five limbs with the general mantra and the heart-seal of all Buddhas.
One immediately becomes the adamantine, indestructible, untainted wisdom of the pure *dharmakāya*.
Taking meditative concentration and wisdom as the sun and moon, one places them within the field of vision and observes with the eye of the *dharmadhātu*.
The eyes illuminate the realms of the ten directions;
as the body is thus, so too is this maṇḍala.
Contemplate the five wheels with this dharma-realm visualization.
First, visualize the fire of wisdom burning away all impurities from the site of the maṇḍala;
its form is as follows.
The mantra of the fire of wisdom is:
Na-maḥ samanta-buddhānām raṃ. Recite this once to burn away the impurities of the ground.
Below this, there is only empty space.
Within that empty space, one further contemplates the wheel of emptiness (*śūnyatā-cakra*).
The shape of this wheel is as shown on the left.
The mantra for contemplating the wheel of space is:
*Namaḥ samantabhadra* (Nā-maṃ-sa-man-da-ta-bha-draṃ). Recite this once. Then, from above the wheel of space, contemplate the wheel of wind.
Its shape is like a crescent moon facing upward and it is black in color;
its form is as shown on the left.
The mantra for visualizing the wind mandala (*vāyu-maṇḍala*) is as follows:
Namaḥ samantabhadra-nātha. First, recite this once; then, from above the wind-mandala, visualize the fire-mandala.
It is triangular and red in color,
its shape as shown on the left.
The mantra of the fire-wheel of the wisdom of observation (*vipaśyanā*) is as follows:
Namaḥ samantabhadrāya. First, recite this once; then, visualize the water wheel above the fire wheel.
It is called the Great Compassion Water Wheel (*mahākaruṇā-udakamaṇḍala*).
It is white like snow or milk, and its shape is like a full moon disk.
Its form is as follows.
The mantra for contemplating the water wheel is:
Na-maḥ saṃmanta-bhadra-āya (1) va-ra-ya (2). Recite this once more. Then, from above the water wheel, contemplate the vajra wheel.
It is square and yellow.
Its shape is as shown on the left.
The mantra for visualizing the Vajracakra is as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabhadra āḥ*. (Recite this once as above. Having thus completed the visualization of the five wheels, empower the ground with the Universal Mantra and its mudrā.
This immediately becomes the true Vajracakra.
Furthermore, one visualizes the assembly of noble ones in the ocean-like gathering of Yuganaddha.
The layout of the maṇḍala is as follows:
Having thus visualized the five wheels and the oceanic assembly of the maṇḍala,
one should recite the universal mantra and empower the ground with the universal mudrā.
It then becomes the ocean-like assembly of the Great Yoga Maṇḍala of the True Vajracakra.
The general mantra is: TĀṂ KHAṂ GHAṂ DHĀTI SAPARA HE MAṄGA GA GA NA KHAṂ SVĀHĀ. This mantra also serves as the general mantra for offerings within the context of worship.
Among the five families, this constitutes the universal offering.
As for the characteristics of the common mudrā:
interlace the ten fingers of the two hands of samādhi and prajñā, aligning them evenly at the joints.
This is the Universal Seal.
If one uses this seal to empower the body,
one immediately attains a vajra-like body that is indestructible.
If one consecrates the ground, it becomes a vajra-ground maṇḍala.
As with the five wheels above,
one briefly contemplates the Maitreya Bodhisattva’s *yogamaṇḍala*.
Within the great luminous orb, further visualize nine luminous orbs as the path of the eight vajra realms.
Among them, the Bodhisattva Maitreya is white in color and wears a crown of the five wisdom Tathāgatas upon his head.
The left hand holds a red lotus flower;
upon the lotus, draw the Dharma-realm Stūpa mudrā.
With the right hand, press the thumb against the fire-wheel on the back of the hand.
With the other fingers extended and slightly bent like a wind-banner,
and emitting various jewel-lights,
he sits in the half-lotus posture upon a precious lotus flower.
Adorned with various necklaces, celestial garments, white sashes, rings, and bracelets,
the four wisdoms, samayas, and so forth are established within the eight luminous circles.
These are explained in detail, item by item, in the chapter on the *maṇḍala* below.

Having visualized as described above, one should perform the rites of the samaya, the expulsion of obstacles, the protection of the body, and the binding of the boundary (sīmābandha) in their proper sequence.
Next, the mantra of the samaya is taught as follows:
Uṃ hūṃ ḍraṃ ḍaṃ liṃ saṃ maṃ ya. As for the form of the mudrā: interlace the ten fingers of the two hands of wisdom (*prajñā*) and concentration (*samādhi*), and join them in *añjali*.
Recite the mantra five times to empower the five places;
one then becomes the samaya-body.
This is called the Samaya Seal of the Heart of All Buddhas.
Because all mudrās are generated by means of this mudrā,
one should first perform the samaya-mudrā.
The mantra for the Vajra Family Samaya is as follows:
*Uṃ vīraṃ vānta traṭ*. As for the mudrā: perform the aforementioned *vajra-añjali* (vajra-clasp) gesture.
Then, join the hands into a fist and place it upon the heart.
While holding the mind within the inner organs,
recite the vidyā seven times.
Open the joined fists and lower both hands three times while binding them;
this is called the Vajradhātu-mudrā.
Having bound [the heart] three times, [it is completed].
By the power of these mantras and mudrās,
one is able to purify the three karmas and stabilize the ground of the mother-mind.
Next, at the site of recitation, one should dispel defilements, contaminations, and obstructing spirits.
In presenting incense, flowers, unguents, powdered incense, and all other ritual implements, one should expel defilements,
manifest pure light, increase majestic power, and establish the Vajradhātu; then,
by binding the boundaries of the various directions, protect oneself and one's companions.
The protection of one’s dwelling place is as described above.
However, regarding matters not yet detailed, when it comes to actual practice, it is essential to recite each mantra and perform each mudrā for protection and sustenance.
This will enable one to achieve accomplishment without any obstacles or difficulties.
One should perform consecration using the mantra and mudrā of the Vidyārāja Trailokyavijaya; each of these is capable of accomplishing all various activities.
Next, recite the mantra of the Vidyārāja Trailokyavijaya as follows:
Oṃ hūṃ vaṃ raḥ haṃ hūṃ; this is the mantra of the Vidyārāja Trailokyavijaya.
Regarding the mudrā for accomplishing all activities:
with the hands of wisdom and concentration, each forms a fist;
extend the index fingers (vāyu-dhvaja) and insert the thumbs (mahā-ākāśa-cakra) into the palms.
It is accomplished by pressing with the three wheels of earth, water, and fire.
As for that mudrā: place the seal of the wisdom-hand upon the heart, and use the seal of the action-hand to touch all objects.
Then, for the boundary of the earth, one should mark the four cardinal directions, the four intermediate corners, and even the zenith and nadir;
by circling three times to the right and pointing at the zenith and nadir, it is accomplished.
Having thus completed the binding of the boundaries of the ten directions:
Next, one awakens the principal deity and all the World-Honored Ones— the four wisdoms and the four pāramitās—
and from the samaya, one arises from meditative absorption to gaze with increasing clarity.
Out of compassion for those who undergo diligent toil, recollecting his former vows, he descends to the site of enlightenment.
The mantra for awakening is:
*Uṃ vīraṃ talaṃ ṣṭa*. As for the characteristics of its hand-seal (*mudrā*): [followed by the description].
With the two hands of Wisdom and Samādhi, join the thumbs (earth-wheels) together in a hook-lock.
Bend the thumbs (great-space-wheels) so that they enter into the palms.
Then, press down upon the thumbs with both the index fingers (water-wheels) and the middle fingers (fire-wheels).
The wind-banner touches it forward;
with the palms facing upward, recite the mantra seven times and,
with the mudrā, initiate from below to invite the deity.
This is called the mudrā for invoking the *iṣṭadevatā* (the chosen deity).
The mantra for invoking the *iṣṭadevatā* is:
Oṃ hūṃ dhaṃ raṃ saṃ maṃ taṃ. As for the characteristics of its hand-gesture (*mudrā*): [The description follows].
Interlace the two hands of Wisdom and Samādhi to form the vajra-fist.
Without releasing this fist, strike the Great Emptiness of Wisdom with the wind-banner of Wisdom;
do the same for the hand of Samādhi.
Thus snap the fingers three times and recite the vidyā seven times;
this constitutes the formal invitation.
In all rituals for requesting the deities to enter meditative absorption,
one should visualize the principal deity in the coral palace of Tuṣita Heaven,
arising from the Samaya of the Universal Manifestation of Form Body (Sarvarūpasaṃdarśana-samādhi).
Descending from the coral palace via the white jewel staircase to the site of practice (maṇḍala),
its form is as follows:
within the Great Perfectly Luminous Sphere.
Furthermore, there are five perfect luminous orbs,
four crescent moon-wheels at the four corners,
and eight precious stupas.
The four vajra-wheels,
the four vajra-scepters,
and the boundary-paths.
In its center is the principal deity, the Bodhisattva Maitreya;
next are the four-faced Prajñāpāramitā Bodhisattvas;
and in the four corners are the four inner offering Bodhisattvas and others.
On the outer edge of that luminous orb,
swirling flames of wisdom-fire descend from space upon those holy beings and others.
All of them wear crowns of the five Tathāgatas of wisdom and each holds their respective hand-seal (mudrā), seated in the half-lotus posture.
These deities, such as Maitreya and the others, are also as described above.
The left hand holds a red lotus flower,
upon which is placed the Dharma-realm stupa mudrā;
the right hand forms the mudrā of preaching the Dharma.
The above is the completion of this.
Having performed the adornment as described above and completed the visualization, one then invites the deity.
The mantra of the Principal Deity is:
Oṃ hūṃ vajra-danda-kuśa-danda (with the vowel *ai* drawn out). As for the characteristics of its mudrā:
Form vajra-fists with both the wisdom and concentration hands;
extend the two wind-banner fingers.
Place the wisdom forearm upon the concentration forearm.
Having formed this mudrā by making a hook-shape directed outward,
recite the mantra seven times.
Once the threefold invitation has been granted and [the deity] has arrived, proceed.
Next, request entry into the maṇḍala.
The mantra for requesting entry into the maṇḍala is:
Oṃ hūṃ vairocana svāhā. As for the characteristics of its mudrā:
Form two vajra fists with the hands of wisdom and samādhi;
extend the two earth-wheels (the little fingers) and interlace the two great space-fingers (the thumbs).
Place the right hand over the left.
Once they have been invited to enter,
recite the vidyā seven times.
Then, having removed the vighnas,
he reveals the samaya and remains there according to the request.
The mantra for requesting him to remain is:
*Oṃ hūṃ jvala krodha aḥ*. As for the characteristics of its mudrā:
Form the vajra-fists with both the wisdom and concentration hands;
extend the two earth-wheels (little fingers) and bend the two great space-wheels (thumbs),
placing them together within the palms.
The foregoing constitutes the invocation;
continuing until [the practitioner] has attained joy and established it firmly,
recite the mantra seventeen times.
The mantra for Firmness is:
Oṃ hūṃ dṛḍha saṃpuṭa ṭaṭha raṭa. As for the characteristics of its mudrā:
Clapping the two hands— the Wisdom and Samādhi hands—
constitutes the Firm Seal (Dṛḍhamudrā).
Next, one should perform the consecration by sprinkling water upon the deity and upon oneself.
The mantra is: Oṃ hūṃ trailokyākṣepa. As for the form of its mudrā:
join the water-wheel (tarjanī) of the wisdom hand with the great space-wheel (aṅguṣṭha).
Hold the remaining wheel upright upon the water vessel and visualize bathing the Honored One. With the mudrā,
sprinkle water upon the crown of the Honored One’s head and your own.
Offer the *argha* perfumed water, visualizing it as being poured upon the crown of the deity’s head.
Form this mudrā and recite the mantra twenty-one times.
2. The Second Chapter on the Offering of Incense, Flowers, and Other Articles to the Deity according to the *Maitreya Bodhisattva Sādhana*. Furthermore, regarding all [beings] of water and land:
Regarding the incense, flowers, precious lamps, ointments, powdered incense, burning incense, scattered flowers,
and so forth that have been prepared: each should be consecrated seven times with the mantra of the respective deity and then offered.
First, offer incense.
The mantra for offering incense is:
*Uṃ vīra-tāra-bhe-e*. As for the mudrā, place the hands in that manner.
Forming two vajra-fists with the hands of wisdom and concentration, place them upon the incense burner.
Recite the mantra twenty-eight times;
it will immediately become a cloud of true, authentic incense.
Pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions,
reaching everywhere,
they extensively perform the Buddha-work.
Next, offer exquisite flowers.
The mantra for offering exquisite flowers is: Oṃ vaṃ dalaṃ puṣpe svāhā. As for the mudrā of this [mantra]:
Forming the vajra-pañjali mudrā with the two hands of wisdom and concentration,
empower them by reciting the mantra seventeen times;
it will then become a true jewel-flower.
Pervading the worlds of the ten directions,
they perform great Buddha-activities and manifest the body of the Jewel Flower Samaya.
Next, the mantra for the offering of the precious lamp is as follows:
Oṃ vaṃ dīpe niści. As for the characteristics of its hand-seal (mudrā): [the mudrā is formed].
Forming vajra-fists with both the wisdom and concentration hands,
extend the two thumbs and place them at the heart.
Recite the mantra seventeen times.
These then become jewel lamps, incense lamps, maṇi-jewel lamps, ghee lamps, incense-flower lamps, and so forth,
filling all worlds throughout the ten directions,
universally offered as offerings of the lamp of wisdom.
Next, the mantra for offering scented unguent is: Oṃ vandanāya hūṃ. As for the form of its mudrā:
With the two hands of Wisdom and Samādhi, cover the palms and extend the eight wheels (fingers).
Press the thumb (great space-wheel) of the right hand upon the thumb of the left hand.
Recite the mantra seven times over this period.
He is identical to the Samaya Bodhisattva of Unguent;
pervading the entire Dharma-realm without exception,
he makes offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.

The aforementioned offerings—incense, flowers, lamps, unguents, and so forth—all become identical to the original Samaya-body, reaching everywhere without exception. Next, one should take refuge in the Triple Gem.

Next, one should confess and repent of transgressions. Next, one should rejoice in merit. Next, one should request that the merit remain forever present. Next, one should generate the mind of Maitreya (the Mother-Earth). Next, one should praise the virtues of the Buddha. Next, one should praise and make sublime, superior vows. Finally, one should extend the mind to make offerings. Regarding those who take refuge in the Triple Gem, it is said:
From this life until I sit upon the seat of enlightenment as a mother, I take refuge in the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed three bodies;

I take refuge in the Dharma-treasury of the Vaipulya Mahāyāna. [I prostrate] three times. I take refuge in the great assembly of all non-retrogressive Bodhisattvas and sentient beings. [I prostrate] three times. One should take refuge in the Three Jewels in this manner.
Regarding those who perform the repentance for expiating transgressions, it is said:
"From beginningless time until this very day,
we have been shrouded and entangled by afflictions."
Furthermore, as we have wandered through birth and death,
we have committed boundless transgressions due to the three kinds of karmic obstructions;
today, with a sincere heart, we reveal and repent of them.
One should extensively repent so as to extinguish all transgressions. Regarding those who pay three prostrations and rejoice in the merit, it is said:
For the sake of sentient beings, the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time [have performed these deeds].
I shall rejoice in all the immeasurable merits they have cultivated. To those who remain permanently, I offer three prostrations and make this request: [Text follows]
I pray that all Buddhas may long remain in the world.
Relying upon the *yuganaddha* principle of non-abiding emptiness (*amogha*), I further entreat you to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma throughout the pure lands of the ten directions.
Regarding the arousal of the Great Mother Ground Mind:
from this day forth until I sit at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa),
I vow to arouse the unsurpassed Great Mother Ground Mind.
"I vow to deliver immeasurable classes of sentient beings,
causing them all to escape and leave behind the ocean of suffering of birth and death;
this is the resolve I have now awakened."
Furthermore, one should remain far removed from the two marks of self and phenomena,
for both self and phenomena are equal in their lack of intrinsic nature.
One should know that this is the mind of the Ground, which gives birth to all.
Empower it with mantras so that the mother-earth’s resolve becomes firm and does not regress.
The mantra for making the mother-earth’s resolve firm and non-regressive is as follows:
Oṃ muditānāmnaye. As for the characteristics of its hand-seal (mudrā): [the description follows].
Form the *vajra-joined palms* (*vajra-añjali*) with the two hands of Wisdom and Samādhi.
Empower them with the *Jñānadhātu-hṛdaya-mantra*,
reciting it seven times.
Next, regarding the praise to be performed, it is said:
recite the mantra of praise as follows.
*Ka-ma-la-mu-ka-ma-la-lu-tsa-na ka-ma-la-sa-tva ka-ma-la-bhaṃ ma-ni-ka-ma-la-ka-ma-la-saṃ-bha-ra sa-ka-la-la-ma-la-krī-la na-bha-si-ti.* Next, one should make the supreme aspiration, saying:
May all sentient beings abound in wealth and treasures.

May they always courageously practice giving out of compassion and be fully endowed with wisdom. May they constantly maintain great patience, cultivate the causes and conditions for virtue, attain the knowledge of past lives, and compassionately care for all living beings.
May all sentient beings, wherever they are born,
obtain such various and supreme things.
Next, one should direct the mind toward making offerings.
By means of mental visualization,
visualize all flowers of the waters and lands— unowned and unappropriated—
filling the void and pervading the entirety of the ten directions.
And with oceans of clouds of exquisite divine and human ointments,
oceans of clouds of burning incense, oceans of clouds of radiant lamps,
and various banners, pennants, precious canopies, and musical instruments.
The *gekabushi* sang of nets of pearls,
with various jeweled bells suspended therefrom,
as well as flower garlands, white whisks, exquisite bells and chimes, and jeweled cords forming a net.
Clouds of wish-fulfilling jewels and garments;
celestial foods of supreme excellence and exquisite fragrance;
and palaces and towers adorned with precious pillars.
With all the celestial ornaments for the body— crowns and necklaces—
and with a mind that increasingly expands to pervade the entirety of space,
one makes such offerings with a heart of utmost sincerity.
It is most excellent. Therefore,
the practitioner should practice this dharma with a concentrated mind.
By offering with a devoted mind,
reciting mantras, and performing mudrās,
all that one has visualized as above will be fully accomplished.
The mantra for the universal mental offering (*manasā-pūjā*) is:
Oṃ hūṃ sarvatathāgate hūṃ vaṃ hīḥ khaṃ ga ga nāṃ jaḥ svāhā. As for the mudrā of this [mantra]: [Description of the hand gesture follows].
Forming the vajra-pañjali mudrā with the two hands of wisdom and concentration,
place them upon the crown of the head and recite this mantra seventeen times;
thus, all implements for offering will be accomplished.
Protect the five places of the body with mantras and mudrās.
Furthermore, visualize a precious lotus flower upon the mudrā;
upon that flower, visualize the seed-syllable for general offerings, which is the syllable *Gan*.
As visualized above,
each and every one flows forth from this single syllable.
Place the seal upon the crown of the head.
Visualize the syllable *saṃ* as golden in color,
emitting light of five great colors;
this is called the seed-syllable gate of offering.

Chapter Three: The Chapter on the Recitation of Mantras for the Practice of Yoga by Maitreya Bodhisattva. If one wishes to quickly attain *siddhi* through Maitreya Bodhisattva, [one should practice as follows].
Without changing the color of his fleshly body, he gazed upon Maitreya with a compassionate countenance;
the latter then rubbed his head, bestowed the prophecy of enlightenment,
and caused him to realize the patience of non-arising and enter the Samādhi of the Universally Manifesting Form Body.
By means of the Maitreya Bodhisattva Dharmadhātu-mudrā,
one empowers the five limbs of both the deity and oneself,
thereby becoming the very essence of Karuṇāmaya.
The mudrā of the Dharmadhātu is as follows:
cross the two earth-wheels and water-wheels within the palms,
with the two wind-banners each resting upon the back of the fire-wheels.
Place the thumbs beneath the fire-wheel [fingers] of the two hands.
With the two middle fingers (the great space-fingers), hold upright the upper joints of the two fire-wheels,
keeping the two fire-wheels approximately one and a half inches apart.
The coming and going of the two wheels of emptiness is thereby accomplished.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Maitreya empowers the deity and the patient with the mantra-seal of the Dharmakāya.
By consecrating the five limbs,
one immediately becomes the pure Dharmakāya.
The Dharma-body mudrā of Maitreya Bodhisattva is as follows:
Interlace the two earth-wheels (thumbs) and bend them into the palms; open the two fire-wheels (index fingers),
extend the two wind-wheels (middle fingers) so they face away from each other,
and bend the two space-wheels (little fingers).
Press both [hands] together at the center of the fire;
when the fire opens up about one and a half inches, the wind-banner moves back and forth.
This is the Dharma-body mudrā of Maitreya Bodhisattva.

ensure that their shapes and appearances do not contradict [the prescribed forms].

Seated in the full lotus posture upon a lotus flower, he enters a state of meditative absorption with a face that is compassionate,
gentle, and smiling, possessing thirty arms,

each representing a distinct samaya;

First, the first left hand holds a lotus flower;
upon the lotus flower, one should draw the seal of the Dharmadhātu Stūpa.

The banner of spreading wind points toward the right cheek,

Next, in the seventh hand on the left, hold a lotus flower;

each time the count reaches one hundred thousand,

one will then receive the instructions of the Honored One.
